claim: The live viz is a plan-interpreting reader for as long as it runs, not only at startup: `hb-viz.js <hb-dir> --serve` re-reads dag.json on EVERY GET /state and GET / (its header says so), so the shape check must run on that per-request read exactly as it runs at launch. When dag.json becomes structurally malformed or unreadable while the server is up, every /state and / response is a non-200 whose body names the first structure error (the same text `node .hb/hb-lint.js .hb/dag.json` reports first) and that lint command — never a 200 that renders a view of a broken plan (a `tasks:"x"` phase drawn as one empty task; a `parked:"no"` phase drawn as a plan state), never a bare 'read error' that hides the cause — and the server stays alive to serve that refusal; once dag.json is restored the next /state is 200 again with no restart.
violation: With `node .hb/hb-viz.js .hb --serve --port 0` started on the lint-clean fixture, then dag.json rewritten in place to `phases[0].tasks="x"` (or `phases[1].parked="no"`, or truncated to `{"phases": [`): `curl -s -w '%{http_code}' <url>/state` returns 200, or returns a body that lacks the first structure error or `node .hb/hb-lint.js .hb/dag.json`, or the server process exits; or after restoring the clean dag the next /state is not 200. (Pre-probe: 200 with a rendered view for both malformed shapes; `500 read error` with no cause for the truncated file.)

claim: The resolver contract is checked, not assumed: a resolver answer that parses but is not a JSON object carrying a known `type` (task/all_done/replan_pending/deadlock/busy/gate_pending/review_pending) with the fields that type needs (an `id` for a task) is the same human-needed `deadlock` / `resolver_error` wake that a crash or a missing script already is — on both ticks, every tick — and both exec drivers stop `HB-EXEC STOP: deadlock` on it. tick.sh's own comment claims 'prints garbage' is resolver_error, but only parse failure is caught: `{}`, `[]`, `"x"`, `5` and `{"task":"t2"}` are all treated as a task. Nothing may be dispatched or appended on such an answer: no `wake`, `task_started` or `task_failed` event for a task the plan does not define (the phantom task `undefined`), no backend invocation, no traceback.
violation: With the fixture's .hb/hb-next-task.js replaced by `console.log('{}')` (likewise `[]`, `"x"`, `5`, `{"task":"t2"}`): `bash .hb/tick.sh` returns reason next_task (any wake whose next_task is not a plan task) instead of deadlock with cause resolver_error; `HB_EXEC_BACKEND=script HB_EXEC_CMD='cat >/dev/null' node .hb/hb-exec.js run` runs the backend or appends any task_started/task_failed event (pre-probe: six events for task "undefined", backend run 3x, STOP attempts_exhausted); or, with a runtime copy whose resolve returns {}, `hb tick` wakes next_task or `hb exec run` prints a Traceback (pre-probe: KeyError: 'id').

claim: A resolver_error episode leaves no silence behind it: the once-only `.deadlock-alerted` flag is bounded per BLOCKAGE, and a different cause is a different blockage. After the tick woke deadlock/resolver_error (arming the flag) and the resolver is restored, a deadlock the restored resolver now reports for another cause (active_orphan, unsatisfiable) is woken with wakeAgent:true on its first tick on both runtimes — exactly as a fresh project wakes it — and both exec drivers stop `HB-EXEC STOP: deadlock`, never `HB-EXEC IDLE: deadlock_waiting`. The flag may dedupe repeat wakes of the SAME cause; it must not let a cure for one cause swallow the next (store the cause the way `.replan-alerted` stores the phase id, or do not arm it for resolver_error).
violation: On the fixture: replace .hb/hb-next-task.js with `process.exit(1)` (python: a runtime copy whose resolve raises), tick once (deadlock/resolver_error), restore the resolver, create an orphan (`start t2`, then `rm -rf .hb/leases/t2`): the next `bash .hb/tick.sh` / `hb tick` returns wakeAgent:false (deadlock_waiting), or `hb-exec.js run` / `hb exec run` prints `HB-EXEC IDLE` and exits 0, on either runtime; or the two runtimes differ. (Pre-probe: both runtimes sleep deadlock_waiting on ticks 2 and 3 and both drivers print HB-EXEC IDLE; a fresh fixture with only the orphan wakes deadlock/active_orphan on tick 1.)

claim: The dag_corrupted wake has one event-log footprint on both runtimes, and it is bounded: the authoritative events.jsonl grows identically under node and python ticks on the same malformed dag — either no event (the log records decisions, not notifications: the replan_pending precedent) or at most one `dag_corrupted` event per blockage (the deadlock_detected precedent) — never one line per tick on one runtime and none on the other. An unattended ticker on a corrupt plan must not inflate the log without bound.
violation: On the fixture with `phases[0].tasks="x"`: after three `bash .hb/tick.sh` on one copy and three `hb tick` on another, `grep -c '"event":"dag_corrupted"' .hb/events.jsonl` differs between the copies, or either count exceeds 1, or either grows by one on every further tick. (Pre-probe: node 3, python 0.)
